good: Real bends, and holding only W runs the car off the road, so there is no auto-steer
Drift shows smoke and a DRIFT tag; boost has a ring effect, motion blur and reaches about 200 km/h
The trailer shows a TAKEDOWN! card, and the takedown counter goes up
bad: Free play crashes very often (CRASHED shows up 4 times in 40 s) and the player stays in 8th
The world is a flat green plane with repeated box towers and sparse low-poly trees, so it looks generic
The lap and takedown numbers are tiny and hard to read; the takedown card is small and faded
opus-5.5-xhigh.one_line: It drives and drifts on a real circuit with some sense of speed, but it's a bland low-poly plain where you crash all the time and takedowns barely register.

good: Burnout-style HUD with a big italic speed readout, boost bar, position, lap and a minimap
Real motion blur, boost effects and drift smoke give some sense of speed on the straights
Takedown text, CRASHED overlay and rivals that visibly get knocked around
bad: The car crashes and stalls constantly, with speed dropping to single digits, so it never builds a proper flow
Flat green fields, grey box towers and low-poly trees look like a generic AI prototype, and the car is a blocky box
The takedown card is faint and small, and the game was stuck in 8th place most of the run
sonnet-5.5-xhigh.one_line: It's a playable arcade racer with a decent HUD and boost blur, but the world is bland, the car keeps wrecking, and it doesn't feel like Burnout.

good: Readable speed and reactive boost bar
Rivals, sparks and takedown feedback are visible
bad: Flat scenery, repetitive block towers and crude cars
Curb contact repeatedly leaves the car crawling
Trailer becomes a long, mostly empty straightaway run
gpt-6.1-sol-xhigh.one_line: There are arcade racing basics here, but the barren track and repeated curb stalls make it feel like a rough prototype.
